item.title: Presence Over Position | The Urgent Kingdom | Mark 9:30-50
item.itunes:title: Presence Over Position | The Urgent Kingdom | Mark 9:30-50
item.description:
What do you want more, a position of importance or the presence of Jesus? In Mark 9:30-50, Jesus is on His way to the cross while His disciples argue about who among them is the greatest. Instead of scolding their ambition, He redirects it, teaching them that true greatness is found not in rank or recognition but in serving without expectation, staying humble, dealing seriously with sin, and living distinctly in a way that brings peace rather than division. God cares about our circumstances, but He is more concerned with the formation of our souls.

Aaron Brockett • The Urgent Kingdom • Mark 9:30-50

item.title: Help My Unbelief | The Urgent Kingdom | Mark 9
item.itunes:title: Help My Unbelief | The Urgent Kingdom | Mark 9
item.description:
In Mark 9, we see two stories: Jesus’ glory revealed to Peter, James, and John, and a desperate father pleading for his son. Two scenes, one truth: because of who Jesus is, every challenge in our lives bows to Him. In this message, Executive Ministries Pastor Chad Lunsford teaches how there is no challenge in our lives that is a match for God's glory. Chad Lunsford • The Urgent Kingdom • Mark 9

item.title: Blurry Faith | The Urgent Kingdom | Mark 8:14-38, 9:1
item.itunes:title: Blurry Faith | The Urgent Kingdom | Mark 8:14-38, 9:1
item.description:
Sometimes our view of Jesus is a little blurry. Mark 8 shows us that spiritual clarity often comes gradually as we learn to trust Jesus, wait on God, and surrender our own way. In this message, Pastor Ryan Bramlett preaches on how Jesus did not come simply to show us how to save ourselves. He came to save us, and He invites us to follow Him by giving up our own way, taking up our cross, and trusting Him by faith.

Ryan Bramlett • Mark: The Urgent Kingdom • Mark 8:14-38, 9:1

item.title: Enough | The Urgent Kingdom | Mark 8:1-13
item.itunes:title: Enough | The Urgent Kingdom | Mark 8:1-13
item.description:
In this message, Carmel Campus Pastor Bart Shaw addresses this question: “Are you seeking Jesus, or just seeking what He can do for you?” He has already done enough. The real question is whether you'll trust Him or keep demanding proof.

Bart Shaw • The Urgent Kingdom • Mark 8:1-13

item.title: Crumbs at God’s Table | The Urgent Kingdom | Mark 7:24-37
item.itunes:title: Crumbs at God’s Table | The Urgent Kingdom | Mark 7:24-37
item.description:
Jesus reveals that His Kingdom is for all people. Through the faith of a Gentile woman and the healing of a deaf man, we see that no one is beyond God's reach. In this message, Pastor Ryan Bramlett teaches how followers of Jesus are called to carry the burdens of others through humble, persistent prayer, trusting that God's grace is more than enough.

Ryan Bramlett • The Urgent Kingdom • Mark 7:24-37

item.title: Why Youʼre Exhausted Even When Youʼre Doing Everything Right | The Urgent Kingdom | Mark 7:1-19
item.itunes:title: Why Youʼre Exhausted Even When Youʼre Doing Everything Right | The Urgent Kingdom | Mark 7:1-19
item.description:
We know rest is essential, and as Christians, we long for the lasting soul rest only God can give. Yet we often chase peace through performance, rules, or appearances. In this message, Guest Speaker Carl Kuhl shows that true rest isn't found in human effort but in surrendering to the overwhelming grace of Jesus Christ.

Carl Kuhl • The Urgent Kingdom • Mark 7:1-19
